summary: Connect named bones to axial and appendicular groupings.
objective: Build a skeletal explorer where selecting a group highlights its bones without losing left/right identity.
example_prompts: Build a skeletal explorer where selecting a group highlights its bones without losing left/right identity.

state_contract.model: Bone identity, anatomical group and laterality; visual hierarchy is not a biomechanical joint model.

invariants: Selection changes emphasis without renaming or reparenting anatomy.
Do not infer mechanical articulation from category membership.
motion_guidance: Use a camera focus or group reveal; keep bone rest positions intact.
Any exploded view preserves reference lines to the rest pose.

A verified mesh and complete naming inventory are required for a comprehensive atlas: the defaults give the adult group totals from the cited section, not a per-bone list, so a scene must still supply names.
The counts are the adult figures; the cited section does not give a newborn or per-region breakdown beyond the axial contents named here.
Authored guidance; no scene runtime or visual verification has run for this recipe.

claims.statement: The appendicular skeleton comprises the limbs and their attachments to the axial skeleton.

For adults there are 206 bones in the skeleton; the axial skeleton of the adult consists of 80 bones including the skull, the vertebral column and the thoracic cage, and there are 126 bones in the appendicular skeleton, which includes all bones of the upper and lower limbs plus the bones that attach each limb to the axial skeleton.
claims.scope: Adult totals for the two divisions and what each division contains. No per-bone inventory, no laterality counts and no developmental variation are claimed.

source_refs.locator: 7.1 Divisions of the Skeletal System: "For adults, there are 206 bones in the skeleton"; "The axial skeleton of the adult consists of 80 bones, including the skull, the vertebral column, and the thoracic cage"; "There are 126 bones in the appendicular skeleton of an adult"; "The appendicular skeleton includes all bones of the upper and lower limbs, plus the bones that attach each limb to the axial skeleton"; "The axial skeleton forms the vertical, central axis of the body and includes all bones of the head, neck, chest, and back"

defaults.rationale: The three totals and the contents of each division restate the cited section (claim.skeletal-hierarchy-bone-counts, claim.skeletal-hierarchy). They exist so the grouping the recipe teaches has an arithmetic consequence a build can check: the two group counts must reconstruct the total, which is exactly the test that catches a girdle filed under the axial skeleton. Nothing here is tunable, because these are counts, not settings, and a scene that models fewer bones should report its own coverage against 206 rather than redefining it.

axial_bones.note: sourced; skull, vertebral column and thoracic cage

appendicular_bones.note: sourced; limbs plus the bones attaching each limb to the axial skeleton, which is where the girdles belong

laterality_values.note: authored bookkeeping category; the section gives no left/right counts

per_bone_inventory.note: 7.1 gives division totals, not a named list of all 206 bones

worked_example.inputs: The two sourced division totals, and a pectoral girdle bone (a scapula) asked to declare its group
worked_example.expected: 80 + 126 = 206, matching the sourced total exactly; the scapula reports appendicular, and moving it to axial breaks the sum by making the axial count 81 and the appendicular 125
worked_example.derivation: 80 + 126 = 206. The girdles attach the limbs to the axial skeleton and the section places attaching bones in the appendicular skeleton, so a scapula is appendicular even though it sits on the trunk - the recipe's stated invariant. The arithmetic is what makes that testable: any misfiled bone leaves the total at 206 but changes both group counts, so a build should assert both group counts and their sum, not the total alone.

tolerance.counts: exact integers; these are inventory totals, not measurements
tolerance.partial_models: a scene modelling fewer bones must report its coverage against 206 rather than asserting a different total
